messages.subject: Ternary plots
parts:
Has anyone implemented ternary plots for ggplot?

They seem like a natural application of the coord system. The only
hard part I can see is how to handle the labelling of the dependent
(third) variable's scale.

-s

PS Hadley wrote in his 2006 presentation that ternary plots didn't fit
into the ggplot framework, but I think that was before coord_xxx was
added to the system.

Yes, that's exactly the problem - how do we add more dimensions to the
coordinate system? One approach would be to add a z position
aesthetic, but that doesn't generalise terribly well for more than 3
dimensions.

On Wed, May 13, 2009 at 9:31 AM, hadley wickham <h.wi...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
>> Has anyone implemented ternary plots for ggplot?
>>
>> They seem like a natural application of the coord system.  The only hard part I can see is how to handle the labelling of the dependent (third) variable's scale.
>
> Yes, that's exactly the problem - how do we add more dimensions to the coordinate system?  One approach would be to add a z position aesthetic, but that doesn't generalise terribly well for more than 3 dimensions.

But in ternary plots, there are only two independent variables; the
third one is 1-x-y.  The problem with the third (dependent) variable
is not how to map it to an aesthetic, but only how to associate a
scale with it to label it properly.

          -s
